h1: Custom Yard Signs for Events, Safety & Marketing
metaDescription: Order custom yard signs for events, safety, and marketing. Durable, double-sided, full color. Bulk pricing available at Perfect Imprints.
introHtml:
Marketing directors planning a neighborhood open house, HR directors rolling out a safety campaign, and business owners promoting a seasonal sale all need one thing: signage that grabs attention fast. Custom yard signs do exactly that. They are a low-cost, high-visibility way to get your message in front of the right people, whether you are advertising a new subdivision, reminding employees of a safety protocol, or directing customers to a pop-up event. With double-sided printing and weather-resistant materials, these signs work in any outdoor setting and can be installed quickly with wire stakes.

Perfect Imprints carries a range of yard sign sizes and customization options to match your specific use case. From 14 1/2" x 23" double-sided signs for short-term promotions to larger 16" x 26" full-color prints for long-running campaigns, you can choose the format that fits your budget and timeline. All signs are made from durable corrugated plastic that withstands wind and rain, and we offer full-color printing, screen printing, and digital printing to bring your design to life. Whether you need 50 signs for a local event or 5,000 for a national rollout, we have the capacity to deliver.
buyingGuideHtml:
When ordering custom yard signs, the first thing to consider is the intended lifespan of your campaign. For short-term events lasting a few days, a standard 14 1/2" x 23" double-sided sign printed on 4mm corrugated plastic is a cost-effective choice. For campaigns that need to hold up for weeks or months, upgrade to a thicker 6mm material or opt for full-color digital printing, which offers better UV resistance. The double-sided feature is essential for signs placed along streets or in high-traffic areas where viewers approach from multiple angles.

Materials and Durability

Most promotional yard signs are made from corrugated plastic, also known as Coroplast. This material is lightweight, waterproof, and resistant to tearing. For added durability, some suppliers offer polypropylene or metal-backed substrates, but these are heavier and more expensive. If your signs will face extreme weather, consider adding a UV-resistant laminate to prevent fading. For indoor or temporary outdoor use, standard corrugated plastic is sufficient and keeps costs low.

Common Use Cases

Marketing directors use branded yard signs for real estate open houses, grand openings, and directional signage at events. HR and safety managers deploy them for workplace safety reminders, traffic flow instructions, and emergency evacuation routes. Business owners rely on personalized yard signs for seasonal sales, political campaigns, and community fundraisers. The versatility of logo yard signs makes them a staple in any promotional toolkit.

Customization and Decoration Options

Screen printing is the most economical option for large quantities of one-color designs. Full-color digital printing allows for photographic images and gradients, ideal for real estate listings or complex logos. For small runs, digital printing offers fast turnaround with no setup fees. Most bulk yard sign orders use screen printing for cost efficiency, while personalized yard signs for local events often use digital printing. Always request a proof to check color accuracy and text legibility.

Quantity and MOQ Guidance

Minimum order quantities for wholesale yard signs typically start at 50 or 100 pieces. As order volume increases, unit price drops significantly. For example, a run of 250 signs might cost half as much per sign as a run of 50. If you are planning a multi-location campaign, it is often cheaper to order a larger quantity once than to reorder in small batches. Lead times for screen-printed signs are usually 5–10 business days, while digital prints can ship in 2–5 days.

Common Buying Mistakes

One frequent error is ordering single-sided signs for street placement. Always choose double-sided printing for public areas. Another mistake is using low-resolution artwork. Yard signs are read from a distance, so text should be large and bold. Avoid small fonts and intricate details. Finally, check the stake type and sign attachment method. Most signs come with wire stakes, but if you are placing them in hard ground, plastic stakes with a pointed end work better. Order a sample first if you are unsure about material or size.

faqs.q: What is the minimum order quantity for custom yard signs?
faqs.a: Minimum order quantities typically start at 50 pieces for screen-printed signs and 25 for digital prints. For bulk orders, we recommend ordering at least 100 units to get the best per-unit pricing.

faqs.q: What sizes are available for yard signs?
faqs.a: Common sizes include 14 1/2" x 23" and 16" x 26". Both are available in single- or double-sided options. Custom sizes may be available upon request for larger quantities.

faqs.q: How long does it take to produce yard signs?
faqs.a: Production lead time is typically 5–10 business days for screen-printed signs and 2–5 business days for digitally printed signs. Shipping time depends on your location and chosen carrier.

faqs.q: Can I get a sample before placing a bulk order?
faqs.a: Yes, we offer sample yard signs for a nominal fee. The sample cost is often credited back if you place a production order. Contact our sales team to arrange a sample.

faqs.q: What is the best printing method for full-color yard signs?
faqs.a: Full-color digital printing is best for photographic images and complex graphics. Screen printing is ideal for one- or two-color designs with large text. Both methods produce durable, weather-resistant signs.
